name: Bleedthrough — The Shared Sorrow Feed
creator: Originated anonymously in the Gray Zone; first documented cluster attributed to a grief circle in the Pilsen Stack, 2207
description: Participants simultaneously opened their BCI emotional-output channels to a shared public feed, broadcasting raw, unfiltered grief — loss of family, debt, eviction, augmentation failure — without context or narration. The trend peaked when hundreds of thousands synced at the same timestamp, creating a cascading empathy overload that briefly overwhelmed commercial feed infrastructure in three Tier 1-3 corridors.
medium: neural feed — open BCI emotional broadcast, mass sync
cultural_impact: Bleedthrough forced public reckoning with what BCI infrastructure actually allowed: the poor broadcasting their suffering directly into the nervous systems of anyone tuned in. Corponation feed regulators scrambled to classify emotional broadcast as 'unstructured data' to justify throttling it.
controversy: HelixCorp and Axiom both lobbied the Meridian Emergency Broadcast Authority to impose 'emotional bandwidth caps' on open BCI channels, framing the trend as a public health risk. the Gray Zone advocates called it the first honest use of BCI in a decade. Three participants required neural detox after sustaining overload injuries during the peak sync.
story_hooks: A character receives a fragment of Bleedthrough grief that lodges in their BCI cache and won't clear — they begin experiencing someone else's memories of a lost child
A Tier 4 corporate feed regulator who helped ban Bleedthrough is tracked down by a the Gray Zone journalist who wants to know what they felt during the peak sync before they switched it off

Someone discovers a bootleg archive of the full peak-sync feed and is selling access — but sustained exposure is causing listeners to lose the ability to distinguish their own emotions from recorded ones
